Markus — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from Redwood's side and proposed next steps so we can size the dedicated pool for OliveTech's streaming use case.

High-level goals we heard today:
- Real-time streaming responses to end-users with partial tokens returned immediately (low tail latency).
- P95 streaming-latency SLO target: 180ms end-to-end for active streams (excluding network hop to client).
- Sustained concurrency target: 400 parallel streaming sessions, with burst tolerance to ~1,000 for short windows (2–5 min).
- Typical response size: 150–350 tokens; heaviest flows can go to ~700 tokens.

What we attached: demo recording + a lightweight latency profile we captured from the test harness (latency_profile_gist.csv).

Initial sizing guidance (ballpark):
- Model family: you mentioned a large open decoder (70B-class) for generation. For those models we typically recommend H100 nodes for peak throughput, or A100 80GB with model sharding for a lower-cost option.
- For the 400 sustained streaming sessions / P95 180ms target we estimate reserved throughput in the neighborhood of 3,000–5,000 tokens/sec depending on batching and kv-cache hit rate.
- If you can quantize to int8 and accept slightly higher latency variance, A100 reserve with aggressive batching hits good cost points. If low tail latency at peak concurrency is the priority, H100 machines with dedicated pools (fewer cross-tenant scheduling effects) are the safer path.

Questions we need answered to firm this up:
1) Which model variant (exact config / tokenizer) will you serve in dedicated?
2) Average tokens-per-response and typical streaming rate per connection (tokens/sec) during active periods.
3) Acceptable cost tradeoffs: prefer lowest monthly commit vs prefer tighter P95?

Proposed next steps:
- Ben to run a 2-hour perf validation with OliveTech prompt-set on our Dedicated preview (we can mirror your workload). Need a sample workload and a scheduled 2-hr window.
- We will produce a short SLO-fit report (latency percentiles, tokens/sec required, GPU utilization estimates) and an updated quote.

I left Aditya and Ben on cc for technical follow-up. If procurement or legal want an initial quote or outline of PO timing, loop procurement in and we can attach a draft (we'll prepare redwood_quote_OLV-2026-023.pdf).

Thanks — Camila

Markus — quick technical notes to answer your questions and propose a short perf plan.

Short answers:
- H100 vs A100: H100 gives better throughput/latency for large attention meshes and long sequences (700 tokens). For your highest-concurrency bursts H100s will reduce queuing and lower P95. A100 80GB can meet the SLO if we shard across multiple cards and lean on kv-cache reuse and quantization (int8/4). L4 is only viable for much smaller models (<=13B) — not applicable here.
- Per-session tokens/sec assumption: our 3k–5k tokens/sec estimate assumes ~8–12 tokens/sec per active stream on average (this models partial-token streaming and CPU/network overhead). So for 400 concurrent streams that maps to roughly 3,200–4,800 tokens/sec. Bursts to 1,000 would push tokens/sec proportionally unless you rely on short-lived bursts with cached prefixes.
- Cache assumptions: estimate assumes ~40–60% effective KV cache reuse across sessions (as you indicated you have many similar prompts). Cache dramatically lowers compute for repeated prefixes and improves latencies for streaming.

Proposed perf validation run (what we'll execute):
1) You send a representative prompt-set (20–50 templates + 200 sample user requests) and expected response lengths.
2) We run three 20-minute phases in our dedicated test pool:
   a) Baseline (A100 80GB pool, int8 quantized variant) at 400 sustained concurrency.
   b) Peak-burst (A100 pool + sharded config) with short 1,000-concurrency bursts to observe queuing/backpressure.
   c) H100 pool run to compare P50/P95/P99 across identical inputs.
3) Collect: latency percentiles, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory occupancy, and streaming stalls.

Deliverables: perf_test_plan.md (attached), a short SLO-fit report, and a recommended reserved-throughput number and GPU topology. We'll also include a short estimate of monthly committed cost for A100 vs H100 options.

Scheduling: we can spin up the test pool as soon as you can provide the sample set and a 2-hour window.
